title: Repair admission shadowing that suppressed short requests during long-context surges
creator: Maya Chen
description: Multiple customers reported sudden 3-6x latency regressions for short, latency-sensitive requests (chat widget / autocomplete) coinciding with background storms of long-context streaming requests (document summarization and large-batch embeddings). Problem manifests across Hosted, Dedicated, and several Private deployments after autoscaler activity. Investigation shows the continuous batcher was entering a transient ‘hold’ state where admission tokens were shadowed by a long-context admission path: a single long-context admission path would acquire a shared admission lease and then perform a delayed credit return under heavy KV/cache churn. While the lease was held, short requests were queued behind a backoff heuristic (idle-backoff + single global admission token) leading to head-of-line suppression. This is distinct from standard prefetch races: the issue is an interaction between the admission lease lifecycle, autoscaler cordon signals, and an aggressive idle-backoff that treated long flows as a signal to reduce admission for the node.
repro_steps: 1) Deploy canary runtime-1.19 on a test Dedicated cluster with two work queues: short-requests (median seq=32) and long-streams (median seq=4096).
2) Start steady short request traffic at 200 qps (latency-sensitive), verify baseline p50/p95,
3) Introduce a surge of long-context streaming requests (20 concurrent, each 4096 tokens) for 30s, repeat every 2 minutes
4) Observe that short-request p95 jumps and queue depth for short-requests grows while GPU utilization stays high but not saturated,
5) Capture admission telemetry: notice single long admission lease with "shadowed_return" events, and global_admission_tokens drop to near-zero during surge.
root_cause_summary: Admission lease reentrancy + delayed token return under KV-churn + autoscaler cordon hysteresis caused the global admission bucket to be starved; an aggressive idle-backoff treated the node as 'dominated' and throttled short-request admission until the lease fully drained.
workarounds: 1) For Hosted: enable per-route explicit fast-path (routing policy) to bypass global admission bucket for latency-sensitive routes (temporary).
2) For Dedicated/Private: reduce idle-backoff multiplier and raise minimum per-len admission floor in cluster config; restart node pools in affected clusters.
3) Apply traffic shaping on client side to smooth long-stream bursts (customer guidance provided).
proposed_fix: Implement length-aware token buckets: maintain two admission pools (latency-sensitive short-pool and long-pool) with weighted refill and fast-preempt path for short-pool when p95 latency exceeds target. Also: remove the 'shadowed_return' path by making token return synchronous on early error paths, and tighten autoscaler cordon->idle-backoff handshake to avoid multi-second hysteresis before admission refill.
changes: scheduler: add short_vs_long admission pools and separation logic (admission/pools.go + admission_test.go)
runtime: convert delayed token return to synchronous path on KV eviction errors (runtime/kv_admission.go)
autoscaler: add cordon release callback to explicitly replenish admission floor (autoscaler/cordon.go)
metrics: new gauges admission_pool_short_tokens, admission_pool_long_tokens, shadowed_return_count, admission_preempt_events
docs: console runbook updates for incident response and per-route fast-path configuration
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic mixed-length load test: under the defined surge pattern steady short-request p95 must be within 1.2x baseline and no queue depth amplification observed
Canary rollout to 3 Dedicated clusters with telemetry: shadowed_return_count must be zeroed and short-pool tokens must not drop below configured floor during surges
No regression in throughput for long-context flows beyond 3% in controlled tests
Playbook lines added to Console runbook and SRE incident steps verified by on-call
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch -> internal CI (unit + integration + admission chaos tests)
2) Nightly synthetic mixed-workload run for 48h on staging cluster
3) Canary roll: deploy runtime-1.19-canary to 3 low-risk Dedicated clusters and one Hosted shard with traffic mirroring for 24h
4) Monitor p50/p95 and new metrics; if stable, progressive rollout to remaining Dedicated clusters over 72h, then Private upgrade windows by request
5) Post-rollout: 7-day observation window and customer follow-up calls with previously escalated accounts
notes: Customer A (Large-SaaS) escalated with reproducible dashboard clip; support ticket #SUP-8721 attached.
Private customer B ran upgrade window concurrently which amplified KV churn - correlates with ENG-41209 note but root cause differs (admission lifecycle vs. state corruption).
We validated that simply increasing global admission tokens reduces impact but doesn't eliminate suppression — separation of pools is required for stable fix.
